answer: In dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect punishment matrices, each vertex in the Sybil tree symbolizes an identity with an associated cost that accrues over time. The expected payoff for multiplying identities diminishes due to cumulative penalties, ensuring that the net gain remains strictly less than zero (\(-\delta\)). This structure converges to a strict Nash equilibrium, where jade identities choose not to Sybil due to anticipated losses.
